title: gate-phase-entry.mjs's in-flight boundary (IN_FLIGHT_MS): now exported, pinned by a derived fixture pair, and its guard comments now assert an outcome property instead of a mechanism
content:
Landed at #63, merged to main as 012db65 (squash of PR #77; source commits c95537a test, 56e8671 fix, 5bdc9bf/a90dd19 Phase 4 fix rounds -- re-derive with `git log --oneline 012db65^1..012db65` on a checkout that still has the source branch, or `git show 012db65 --stat`). Two things changed; keep them separate because #63's own spec drew the line sharply.

WHAT CHANGED MECHANICALLY (R1/R3/R4/R6). `IN_FLIGHT_MS` (`plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs:165`, value unchanged at `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`) is now `export const`, not module-private; `inFlight()` itself is deliberately NOT exported (re-derive: `git grep -n 'export.*inFlight' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` -- zero hits by design, see the survivor note below). test-gate-phase-entry.sh now reads the constant once at suite start via the same dynamic-import path probe43 already used, and derives a boundary PAIR of fixture ages from it rather than the old fixed 1h/25h literals: INSIDE = now - (IN_FLIGHT_MS - MARGIN) (refuses), OUTSIDE = now - (IN_FLIGHT_MS + MARGIN) (abstains, reason 'is not in flight'), MARGIN = 300000ms (5 minutes) pinned by the spec's two-sided rule. The INSIDE cell's wall-clock elapsed time between writing the fixture and the gate returning is ASSERTED below MARGIN, not printed, so a slow runner fails loudly instead of flaking. A non-zero control drives the identical two fixtures against a SHIFTED-boundary copy of the guard placed OUTSIDE the checkout (a scratch tmpdir): both cells must read `not-applicable` there, proving the control discriminates a broken copy (which would fail open to silence) from a correctly-shifted one. Runtime behaviour of the shipped guard is otherwise byte-identical to pre-#63: a 14,560-cell sweep and a 50-blob corpus replay both found zero decision changes versus the pre-#63 guard, each replay backed by its own non-zero control. TWO EXPECTED SURVIVORS ARE DECLARED, not accidental: the guard's own `<=` vs `<` at the boundary, and probe43's `>` vs `>=` on the same boundary from the other side. Neither is pinnable through the CLI path, because the guard reads its own `Date.now()` inside a CHILD PROCESS started after the fixture file is already written, so the test driver cannot inject the guard's clock value; both survivors are recorded as review obligations on any future edit to `inFlight`'s `now` argument, not as mechanized guarantees (SecOps's residual: an override threaded into `inFlight`'s `now` ARGUMENT at its call site, gate-phase-entry.mjs:538, would leave R1's three cheap module-shape assertions green while making the guard's clock millisecond-exact from outside -- filed as a review obligation, not closed).

WHAT CHANGED IN THE PROSE, AND WHY THIS IS THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING PAST THIS ISSUE. Before #63, the guard's header (:26-27) and `inFlight`'s own doc comment (:490-491, now renumbered) each asserted a MECHANISM claim about the relationship between this guard's 24h window and pipeline-status.mjs's own 'possibly stuck' filter. Every one of four successive drafts written during #63 to correct that claim was ITSELF measurably false, and the test suite was green through all four, because the suite pins that a sentence was removed and where its replacement sits, never what the sentence asserts:
  1. 'the guard reuses pipeline-status.mjs's definition rather than inventing a second one' -- false: no shared symbol exists anywhere in the tree; each module holds its own independent 24h/verdict literal.
  2. 'an undatable record is neither stuck there nor in flight here' -- false: pipeline-status.mjs substitutes the status.json FILE MTIME for an absent-or-null `updated_at` (`updated_at: status?.updated_at ?? mtime`, pipeline-status.mjs:101) before comparing, so an absent-or-null `updated_at` fires BOTH predicates (this guard abstains, pipeline-status reports 'possibly stuck'). Because `??` fires only on absent/null, an UNPARSEABLE STRING is the one undatable spelling the two modules still agree on.
  3. 'the two date functions agree on ISO strings and diverge on anything else' -- false: `new Date(string)` delegates to `Date.parse`, so the two agree on EVERY string, ISO or not ("March 3, 2020", "2020/03/03", "not-a-date" all land identically in both). They part only on non-string values, and not even all of those: `updated_at: 12345` reads here as the year 12345 (permanently in flight), while pipeline-status.mjs's `stuck` filter is never reached on any code path for that value -- markdown mode throws first (in `listActive`'s sort comparator or `renderMarkdown`'s table loop, depending on readdir order) and `--json` mode never calls `renderMarkdown` at all.
  4. a fourth draft (about `listActive`'s sort-comparator throw ordering with multiple issue dirs) was also falsified: `localeCompare` coerces its ARGUMENT, so only a bad RECEIVER throws; readdir position governs which dir throws, not dir count, and the throw is not even cleanly 'not last' since binary insertion probes only an O(log n) prefix of the array.
  THE FIX THAT SHIPPED (R2/AC12) stops enumerating the mechanism and asserts only the OUTCOME PROPERTY that held across every measured cell: pipeline-status.mjs's `stuck` filter is not reached on any path for a value this guard treats as in-flight-forever, full stop -- no claim about WHY, no claim about which comparator throws first, no claim about ISO-vs-non-ISO. Both comment sites (header :26-27-ish and `inFlight`'s doc comment) now read this way; re-derive current wording with `git show 012db65:plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs | sed -n '20,32p;505,524p'`. THE GENERALISABLE RULE: when a claim about a mechanism keeps turning out false at the edges, stop enumerating the edges more carefully and describe the guaranteed OUTCOME instead. A mechanism you cannot pin down should be characterised by what it guarantees, not by when it fires. See the companion decision record `knowledge/decisions/assert-outcome-property-not-mechanism.json` for this as a standalone rule.

OPEN, ROUTED ELSEWHERE, NOT THIS FILE'S JOB TO RESTATE. Issue #74 tracks every other spelling of the '24h in flight / possibly stuck' number and claim across the tree; #63 fixed the two Lane-1 sites here (R2) and routed the rest there. AT #63's OWN PHASE 5, a knowledge-drift claim was filed (via impl-report.json, routed to the Librarian because #74 is cited FROM shipped code and the shipped comment's correctness now depends on #74's content being right) that #74 as currently written UNDER-COUNTS: it records only ONE module reading a different column than this guard (session-start.sh's `find -mtime -1` over file mtime) and treats pipeline-status.mjs's filter as this guard's exact complement. Live reality, verified above in this same entry: TWO modules read a different column (pipeline-status.mjs's mtime-substitution is not a complement, it agrees with this guard only on the unparseable-string case), and a THIRD divergence (the date-parse function itself, `Date.parse` vs `new Date().getTime()`) is not recorded in #74 at all. This entry now carries the corrected count so a reader here gets it right regardless of #74's own staleness; #74 itself was not edited by the Librarian (issues are not part of the knowledge store) and should be corrected by whoever triages it next -- flagged in this run's drift_flags.

QA's separately-filed ruling (issue #74, not restated here, see that issue) is that the CONTENT half of a claim like the four above IS mechanizable if the check targets the PROPOSITION against live modules rather than the comment TEXT; a text-diff check only proves a sentence moved, not that it is true. Point at #74 for the two checks and their non-zero controls rather than re-deriving them here.

ADDENDUM AT #106 (merged fc9a171): the predicate this entry describes moved OUT of `inFlight()`'s own body and into a new shared leaf module, `plugins/pipeline/scripts/run-candidates.mjs` (`inFlightObservations`). `inFlight()` itself is STILL not exported (`function inFlight`, gate-phase-entry.mjs:549, re-derive: `git grep -n 'export.*inFlight' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs` still zero hits) and its body is now a one-line delegation: `return inFlightObservations(status, now, IN_FLIGHT_MS).inFlight;`. `IN_FLIGHT_MS` itself is UNCHANGED: still declared at gate-phase-entry.mjs:189, still `export const`, still `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`, still the value test-gate-phase-entry.sh's boundary-pair fixtures derive from -- #106 added a SECOND consumer of the same predicate (hooks/pre-tool-use-resolve.mjs, via run-candidates.mjs), and a new suite (test-pretooluse-inflight-ceiling.sh) pins the module's own default copy of the constant equal to gate-phase-entry.mjs's authoritative one, so the two declarations cannot drift silently. This does NOT contradict this entry's earlier claim that 'no shared symbol exists anywhere in the tree' -- that claim was scoped to a comparison against `pipeline-status.mjs`, which #106 left untouched and which still holds its own independent 24h/mtime-substituted literal with no shared symbol. See `architecture--pretooluse-tracked-write-gate.json` for the full account of the new module and its two consumers.
